meta.title: Development of an extrusion-based 3D-printing strategy for clustering of human neural progenitor cells.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: A fibrin/alginate/genipin bioink (based on the Willerth lab formulation) was printed on a BIO X at low pressure to cluster human neural progenitor cells into lattices.

formulations.crosslinking: 20 mg/mL CaCl2 + 1.7 µg/mL thrombin + 0.75 mg/mL chitosan
formulations.name: UTEP bioink: fibrin + HV/MV alginate + genipin
formulations.composition_detail: 20 mg/mL fibrin, 20 mg/mL HV alginate, 10 mg/mL MV alginate, 0.3 mg/mL genipin
formulations.key_outcome: Low-pressure printing (21 kPa) of a fibrin/alginate ink formed clustered neural progenitor lattices.

evidence.quote: final concentrations of 20 mg/mL fibrin, 20 mg/mL high viscosity (HV) alginate (#154724, MP Biomedicals-ThermoFisher Scientific), 10 mg/mL medium viscosity (MV) alginate, and 0.3 mg/mL genipin
Low extrusion pressure of 21 kPa was used to ensure cell viability and create lattice patterns designed with SolidWorks (Concord, MA) at 2 mm/s
Solutions of the crosslinker were prepared to have final concentrations of 20 mg/mL CaCl2, 1.7 μg/mL thrombin, and 0.75 mg/mL chitosan.
